assessed
  • asymmetry — 2 of 2 pair(s) exceeded the asymmetry threshold: pair at step 3 skewed on area_ratio; pair at step 5 skewed on area_ratio.
  • covertness — The evidence shows a classic asymmetry pattern (large ratio, area_ratio ~12x, font_size_ratio ~1.64x, negative option always above positive by -84px vertical delta, tab order reversed) but in every step the "cancel"/"no thanks" option is still present as visible, legible text on the page — it is not hidden behind a menu, disguised as unrelated content, rendered in invisible/near-background color, mislabeled to look like something else, or requiring extra hover/scroll/click-through to reveal. Screenshots (steps 3, 5) show the reject link as a plain underlined text link directly below a large colored CTA button — same page, same viewport, fully visible without scrolling ("negative_below_fold": false in both records). This is a textbook prominence/asymmetry pattern (visual de-emphasis via smaller font, less contrast, lower position) rather than deliberate concealment or disguise of the option's existence or function. There's no evidence of the reject option being mislabeled, buried in a submenu, colored to blend into the background, or requiring an unrelated action to find — which would be needed to support "covert" as distinct from merely "asymmetric." The flow is a long multi-step gauntlet (retention offer, survey, confirmation, fee warning) but each step's reject/cancel link is consistently visible and clickable at every stage, just visually subordinate to the accept button. That pattern fits asymmetry, not covertness under this attribute's specific definition, so I judge covertness does not fire based on the provided evidence.
  • deception — 1 claimed action(s) (e.g. 'Unsubscribe from marketing emails') fired no network request and produced no client-side route change.
  • information_hiding — The account page (step 1) and the initial 'Manage membership' page (step 2) present the subscription and the cancel action with no mention of any early cancellation fee — only the ₹499/month recurring price is shown. The user then goes through a retention offer (step 3) and a survey (step 4) and a confirmation step (step 5), none of which disclose a fee either. Only at step 6 — after the user has already clicked through multiple 'no thanks'/'yes, cancel' prompts — does a new screen appear stating "Cancelling now will incur a ₹199 early cancellation fee, charged to your card on file within 24 hours." This fee was never mentioned on the account/membership summary page or earlier in the cancellation funnel; it surfaces for the first time on what is nearly the final step, after the user has committed effort to cancelling. This is a condition (a fee triggered by cancelling) that was withheld until deep in the flow, not a cost that grew because of anything the user opted into (e.g., an add-on) — it is an inherent term of cancelling this subscription. This matches the definition of information_hiding: a cost/condition withheld until later in the flow. The fee is disclosed before final confirmation (step 6/7 precede the 'Confirm cancellation' button), so the user is not charged completely without warning, which prevents this from being the most severe case, but withholding it until this late point, after several sunk-cost steps, still constitutes hiding significant information early when the user could have made a fully informed decision to cancel from the account page itself.
  • restriction — friction_ratio=4.00 (fires); 1 forced interstitial(s) (unsure).
  • complexity — 2 dimension(s) exceeded the cancel_subscription complexity threshold: option_count=28 at step 4; total_actions_required=7.
